headline: UK’s Healey Backs Heathrow Third Runway in Clash With Burnham
author: Philip Aldrick

paragraphs.text: Fri, October 16, 2026 at 2:30 PM PDT 2 min read
(Bloomberg) -- Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey has backed plans for a third runway at Heathrow, setting up a possible Downing Street clash with Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

Speaking to reporters at the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings in Bangkok the chancellor made his support for the project clear, saying "the case for a third runway at Heathrow has always been a case for growth."

Burnham has refused to state whether he would back expansion of the UK's premier airport, arguing that "it's a matter for London and Londoners," and that he is "open minded" about the £49 billion ($65 billion) plan.

Healey is backing the current scheme and voted for the third runway in a parliamentary vote on new capacity in 2018. Their contrasting positions are the first sign of potential tensions between the chancellor and his more illustrious neighbor at 10 Downing Street.

Approving a third runway at Heathrow was the centerpiece of former Chancellor Rachel Reeves' plan for growth and investment. She committed to the long-awaited, much debated project in January last year when Keir Starmer was prime minister. She said at the time she wanted planning to be "signed off" before the next election, due on 2029.

Reeves set a target of completing Heathrow expansion by 2035, but airport chiefs have said it may not be up and running until 2039. Thomas Woldbye, Heathrow's chief executive, said it would be a "huge missed opportunity" if the runway was not built. The investment would simply go elsewhere in the world, he said.

The Department for Transport estimates that an expanded Heathrow would create 60,000 local jobs and deliver as much as £42 billion of benefits to the UK. The UK's Climate Change Committee is being consulted on how to ensure expansion is consistent with the net zero framework.
